tests.name: prose
tests.output: Sunlight contains all colors of visible light, but when it enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in all directions. Shorter wavelengths of light—like blue and violet—scatter much more than longer wavelengths like red. Because blue light scatters across the sky so effectively, our eyes perceive the sky as blue.

tests.name: prose
tests.output: Sunlight contains all colors, but when it enters the atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in different directions. Shorter wavelengths of light—like blue and violet—scatter much more than longer wavelengths such as red. Because blue light scatters across the sky in every direction, our eyes receive it from all over, making the sky appear blue.
